strings.name: Remo Ruffini
strings.role: Moncler Executive Chairman, responsible for group creative direction
strings.summary: After founding New England, Remo Ruffini acquired Moncler in 2003 and advanced its development from mountain apparel into an international luxury business. He was involved in its listing, Moncler Genius and the Stone Island acquisition. In April 2026, he handed the CEO role to Leo Rongone, remaining Executive Chairman with responsibility for creative direction.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 17 November 2026. Distinguish acquirer from brand founder, Executive Chairman from CEO, agreement from closing, and ownership percentages in Double R from those in Moncler. Older CEO descriptions are not used as his current role.
strings.influence.rationale: Acquired and reshaped Moncler, developing the down-jacket brand into an international luxury business.
strings.facts.f1.label: Early experience
strings.facts.f1.value: Studied and trained in Italy and the United States and worked in clothing alongside his father Gianfranco; no specific degree was verified.
strings.facts.f2.label: Current responsibilities
strings.facts.f2.value: Since 1 April 2026, retains Executive Chairman and creative-direction responsibilities; Bartolomeo “Leo” Rongone serves as group CEO.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Brand repositioning and creative collaboration
strings.highlights.h1.text: Advanced an international luxury positioning centered on down jackets and brought multiple creators into Genius; he did not personally design every collection.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Group expansion and shareholder partnership
strings.highlights.h2.text: Stone Island joined the group upon acquisition closing in 2021; in 2024, LVMH partnered with his holding company through investment in Double R.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Recent interview published
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed New York retail strategy; date denotes publication.
strings.timeline.t2.title: CEO handover
strings.timeline.t2.text: Leo Rongone became CEO; Ruffini remained Executive Chairman with responsibility for creative direction.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Shareholding partnership with LVMH
strings.timeline.t3.text: An LVMH entity acquired 10% of Double R, not a direct 10% of Moncler.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Stone Island acquisition closing
strings.timeline.t4.text: Moncler completed the transaction announced in December 2020, bringing Stone Island into the group.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Launch of Moncler Genius
strings.timeline.t5.text: The company used collaborations with multiple creators to reinterpret the brand and broaden creative expression.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Moncler listing in Milan
strings.timeline.t6.text: The company entered the Italian stock market, a capital-market milestone in its international development.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Acquiring Moncler
strings.timeline.t7.text: Took over a decades-old brand and advanced its global luxury positioning, rather than founding the brand.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founding New England
strings.timeline.t8.text: After returning to Italy, began with men’s shirts before expanding into sportswear.
